Case of the petitioners 3.
It is the case of the petitioners that on 25.03.2021, the deceased along with his friends Rohit and Bunty were proceeding towards his residence on the scooty bearing registration No. DL-4SCH-8124.

When they reached Dasgarha Village ahead of red light, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1PD-0794 which was being driven by the respondent no. 1 at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit them with great force due to which they sustained grievous injuries.
It is further stated that the deceased was taken to Dr. RML Hospital where his MLC was prepared and he was declared brought dead by the doctors.
Case of respondent no. 1 4.
Respondent no. 1 did not file his reply to the claim petition despite opportunity being given.
Case of respondent no. 2 5.
Respondent no. 2 filed its reply to the claim petition wherein it is stated that the deceased had met with the alleged accident due to his own fault.
It is further stated that the accident did not occur due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1.
It is further stated that the deceased and his friends were not wearing helmets and none of them had driving license as they all had not attained the age of majority.

It is further stated that as per mechanical inspection report of the vehicle of deceased, they had hit the alleged offending vehicle on its rear side as the alleged offending vehicle was stationary at the bus stop and the deceased along with his friends were coming from behind at a high speed and hit the stationary vehicle.
It is further stated that the police has not conducted proper investigation and has not mentioned the correct facts in the FIR.
It is further stated that the alleged offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no. 3 w.e.f. 29.08.2020 till 28.08.2021.
It is further stated that the alleged offending vehicle was having valid permit and fitness on the date of accident.
It is further stated that the bus was being driven by a competent driver having a valid and effective driving license.

Respondent no. 3/Insurance Company filed its written statement to the claim petition wherein it is stated that the deceased was a minor child and hit the stationary bus from the back side when the bus was stopped at Bus Stop at Dasgarha.
It is further stated that the accident took place due to sole negligence of deceased.

On 05.11.2022, the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-

14. The findings on the aforementioned issues are rendered hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs.

ISSUE NO. 1 - Whether the deceased Suraj sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 25.03.2021 at about 9:05 PM, ahead of traffic light of NASC Dasgarha Village, Todapur,
New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No.DL-1PD-0794 being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no. 3?

OPP. 
15.
Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
The petitioner no. 2 has examined himself as PW1.
During cross- examination, he admitted that he is not an eye witness to the accident.
Since PW1 is not an eye witness to the accident, his testimony cannot be considered for determining if the bus was being driven rashly and negligently.
16. The petitioners examined Sh. Sameer @ Bunty as PW2.
He deposed that he along with his friends Rohit Prasad and Suraj were proceeding towards his residence on the scooty bearing registration No. DL-4SCH-8124.
He further deposed that the scooty was being driven by his friend Rohit Prasad with due care and caution, following traffic rules and regulations and on the proper and correct side of the road.

He further deposed that when they reached Dasgarha village ahead of red light Bus stop, the offending vehicle, i.e. cluster bus bearing registration No. DL-1PD-0794,
which was being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit him and his friends with great force.
He further deposed that they sustained grievous injuries all over their body.
He further deposed that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle.
17. During cross-examination, he deposed that they were minors and were not holding valid driving license at the time of accident.
He further deposed that he had noted down the vehicle number and routed number at the time of accident.
He further deposed that the bus came from behind and applied brakes suddenly due to which the accident took place.
He further deposed that their scooty Ranju Devi And Ors. (Fatal Case) vs Ashutosh Mishra And Ors.

4 was being driven at a slow speed and hit at the back side of the bus.
He further deposed that there is only damage in the front side of the scooty and no damages on either side of the scooty.
He further deposed that his statement was not recorded by the police.
He further deposed that they all were wearing black helmets at the time of accident.
18. SI Dinesh Singh, who was the first IO of the present case, was examined as R3W1 in the connected matter.

During cross- examination, he deposed that the alleged offending vehicle was stationary at the bus stop and as per investigation, the victims were minor at the time of accident and they had hit the alleged offending vehicle on its rear side.
He further deposed that he received PCR call about the accident vide DD No. 79A dated 25.03.2021.

He further deposed that he along with constable Naresh reached at the spot of accident and saw that the bus was stationary not in proper way at the bus stop and one scooty was lying down under the rear part of left side of the bus.

He further deposed that he did not find any rash and negligent driving on the part of driver of the scooty and the injured Bunty informed that the bus was stopped suddenly by its driver due to which collision took place between the scooty and bus.
He deposed that the driver of the bus suddenly turned his bus in a wrong direction and then suddenly stopped the bus due to which the scooty collided with it.
He further deposed that the damage on the scooty was from front and left side.
He further deposed that the injured was not having the driving license and as per MLC, all the injured were minor.
He further deposed that he had prepared the Kalandra against Bunty for triple riding on the scooty.
19. As per chargesheet, FIR and testimony of IO examined as R3W1, the cluster bus bearing registration No. DL-1PD-0794 was wrongly parked and one scooty was under the rear part of the bus.
20. Perusal of site plan reveals that the cluster bus was at NASC Bus Stop when the accident took place.
Therefore, it cannot be said that it had been parked at a wrong place.
21. There is no material on record which establishes as to what was wrong in the manner in which the bus was parked.
The assertion that the bus was wrongly parked is vague.
It was necessary to establish as to what was wrong in the way it was parked.
22. Mere assertion that the vehicle was wrongly parked is not sufficient for this Tribunal to conclude that the bus was rashly and negligently parked wrongly.
23. The only eye witness examined in the present case is one of the victims, i.e. Sameer @ Bunty examined as PW2.
There are contradictions in his testimony.

In his evidence by way of affidavit, he deposed that when he along with his friends reached the bus stop on their scooty, the bus which was being driven in a rash, negligent and reckless manner and at a high speed, came and hit the scooty.
In his cross-examination, he denied the suggestion that the bus was stationary at the bus stop.
He deposed that the bus was coming from behind and suddenly applied brakes which caused the accident.
It appears that what PW2 meant to say is that the bus overtook the scooty and then suddenly applied brakes due to which the scooty collided with the bus.
However, this cannot be interpreted to mean that the bus "came" and hit the scooty.
There is no coherence in the testimony Ranju Devi And Ors.

5 of this sole eye witness, which is also not in consonance with the other material on record on the manner in which the accident took place.
24. The assertions made in the evidence by way of affidavit are that the bus came and hit the scooty.
This is in contradiction to the assertion that the bus overtook the scooty and was suddenly stopped due to which the scooty struck against the bus from behind.
25. There is no consistency in the statements on record on how the accident took place.
It cannot be held that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the bus.
This issue is accordingly decided against the petitioners and in favour of the respondents.
ISSUE NO. 2 - Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
26.

Since issue no.1 has been decided against the petitioners and in favour of respondents, the petitioners are not entitled to any compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act dealing with 'fault liability', under which the present claim petition has been filed by them.
27. Accordingly, this Tribunal deems it appropriate to convert the present claim petition to Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act for granting compensation under the 'no fault liability' provision.

However, the question arises whether the Tribunal has powers to suo moto convert a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act to Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
28.

In this regard, reliance is placed upon the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Shiv Prasad Indramani & Anr., MAC Appeal No. 194 of 2021,
decided on 27.05.2024.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Shiv Prasad Indramani & Anr., MAC Appeal No. 194 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the Tribunal had dismissed the claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
While doing so, it suo moto converted the case to one under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act and awarded compensation under the no fault liability clause.
The Award was assailed before the Hon'ble High Court.
It was argued that the Tribunal did not have suo moto powers to convert the claim petition under Section 166 to Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It was pointed out that no application was filed for conversion of the case.

29. However, the Hon'ble High Court held that the Tribunal can suo moto exercise powers for conversion of claim petition under Section 166 to Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act and the jurisdiction of the Tribunal would not depend merely on moving of an application by the claimants for conversion.

It was observed that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation and therefore, endeavour has to be as to how best the intention of legislation can be achieved so as to safeguard the interest of victims of the accident.
30.
In view of the above Judgment, the present claim petition under Section 166 is converted to no fault liability provisions of Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
31. As per above provisions, a fixed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- is payable in case of death.

Kashmiri Lal 2007 ACJ 688, this compensation shall be recovered by attaching the bank account of respondent no. 3 with a cost of Rs.5,000/-.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
19. As per chargesheet, FIR and testimony of IO examined as R3W1, the cluster bus bearing registration No. DL-1PD-0794 was wrongly parked and one scooty was under the rear part of the bus.
20. Perusal of site plan reveals that the cluster bus was at NASC Bus Stop when the accident took place.
Therefore, it cannot be said that it had been parked at a wrong place.
21. There is no material on record which establishes as to what was wrong in the manner in which the bus was parked.
The assertion that the bus was wrongly parked is vague.
It was necessary to establish as to what was wrong in the way it was parked.
22. Mere assertion that the vehicle was wrongly parked is not sufficient for this Tribunal to conclude that the bus was rashly and negligently parked wrongly.
This is in contradiction to the assertion that the bus overtook the scooty and was suddenly stopped due to which the scooty struck against the bus from behind.
It cannot be held that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the bus.
Since issue no.1 has been decided against the petitioners and in favour of respondents, the petitioners are not entitled to any compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act dealing with 'fault liability', under which the present claim petition has been filed by them.
27. Accordingly, this Tribunal deems it appropriate to convert the present claim petition to Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act for granting compensation under the 'no fault liability' provision.
However, the question arises whether the Tribunal has powers to suo moto convert a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act to Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
28.
In this regard, reliance is placed upon the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Shiv Prasad Indramani & Anr., MAC Appeal No. 194 of 2021,
decided on 27.05.2024.
In the said case, the Tribunal had dismissed the claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
